meaning: The number 37 appears in the Bible in connection with David's mighty men, Jehoiachin's exile, and chronological notes. In Kabbalistic tradition, it is linked to the unity of the soul and divine wholeness.
description: The most well-known biblical occurrence of 37 is in 2 Samuel 23:39, where David's mighty warriors are counted as thirty-seven. These heroes formed the core of David's military leadership and symbolize loyalty and courage in service to the anointed king. Another important occurrence is Jehoiachin's release from captivity in Babylon after 37 years (2 Kings 25:27; Jer 52:31). This event concludes both the Books of Kings and Jeremiah, serving as a glimpse of hope – David's royal line was not completely wiped out but was lifted up again after a long time in exile. The number also appears in genealogical contexts, such as Levi's lifespan of 137 years (Exod 6:16) and in dating the reigns of kings (2 Kings 13:10). In Kabbalistic tradition, 37 is connected to the concept of 'yechidah' (יחידה), the highest part of the soul, which has a gematria value of 37. Although the number carries richer meaning in this tradition, it does not play a prominent independent symbolic role in Scripture compared to numbers like 7, 12, or 40.

versions.meaning: The number 37 has limited direct symbolic meaning in the Bible but is associated in Jewish numerology (gematria) and Kabbalistic tradition with wisdom, the unity of the soul, and divine wholeness.
versions.description: In Kabbalistic tradition, 37 is associated with the concept of 'yechidah' (יחידה), which denotes the highest part of the soul and has a gematria value of 37. Mathematically, 37 is a factor in 111 (37×3), and multiples of 37 form repeating digits (111, 222, 333, etc.), which in Kabbalistic thought are interpreted as expressions of divine unity and wholeness. In the Bible itself, the number appears in certain genealogical and chronological contexts – for example, Jesus can be counted as the 37th generation from David in one counting within Luke's genealogy (Luke 3:23–38). Nevertheless, 37 does not play a prominent independent symbolic role in Scripture compared to numbers such as 7, 12, or 40. It is important to distinguish between biblical number symbolism and later Kabbalistic-numerological tradition when considering the meaning of this number.

footnotes.text: David's 37 mighty men are listed in 2 Samuel 23:8–39 and in a parallel list in 1 Chronicles 11:10–47. The lists differ somewhat from each other in number and names.

Jehoiachin's release in the 37th year of exile (2 Kings 25:27; Jer 52:31) is the last event recorded in the Books of Kings. Many scholars see this as a theological marker that God's promises to David's house were not forgotten.

The term 'yechidah' (יחידה) denotes, in Kabbalistic soul doctrine, the highest of the five levels of the soul and represents complete unity with the divine. The gematria value is י(10)+ח(8)+י(10)+ד(4)+ה(5) = 37.

Mathematically, 37 is a factor of 111 (37×3), and multiples of 37 form repeating digits (111, 222, 333, etc.). In Kabbalistic thought, this is interpreted as an expression of divine unity and repetition.

Some have attempted to count Jesus as the 37th generation from David in Luke's genealogy (Luke 3:23–38), but this depends on which names are included and how one counts, and it is not widely accepted.
